what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat HIV-1 infection in adults and children who weigh at least 35 pounds (14 kg). It helps lower the amount of HIV virus in your blood (called your viral load) and raises the number of CD4 cells (infection-fighting cells) in your body. This helps your immune system work better. This medicine does NOT cure HIV, but it helps you stay healthier and lowers your chance of getting infections or other HIV-related illnesses. You can still pass HIV to others, so always practice safe sex and do not share needles.
how_to_take: Take ONE tablet by mouth ONCE a day WITH a meal. Eating food is very important — food helps your body absorb this medicine properly. Do not take it on an empty stomach. Swallow the tablet whole. Do not crush, split, or chew the tablet. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual dose for adults and children weighing at least 35 pounds (14 kg) is one tablet once daily with a meal. Your doctor will confirm the right dose for you or your child. Do not take more or less than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been LESS than 12 hours since your scheduled dose time, take it right away with food. If it has been MORE than 12 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time with a meal. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one. Missing doses can cause the virus to become harder to treat, so try your best not to miss any.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the medicine in the original bottle with the cap tightly closed. Keep it away from moisture and heat — do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the bottle.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids (like Tums or Maalox) within 2 hours before or 4 hours after your dose, as they can make this medicine less effective. Do not take proton pump inhibitors (like omeprazole or pantoprazole) because they should NOT be used with this medicine. Do not take H2 blockers (like famotidine or ranitidine) except under specific timing instructions from your doctor. Avoid St. John's Wort (an herbal supplement) — it can make this medicine stop working. Tell ALL of your doctors and pharmacists about every medicine, vitamin, supplement, or herbal product you take. Do not drink large amounts of alcohol. Do not share this medicine with anyone else.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get medical help right away if you notice: yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), dark or tea-colored urine, pale stools, stomach pain or nausea that does not go away, feeling very tired or weak, muscle pain or weakness, trouble breathing, symptoms of a new infection such as fever or swollen glands, mood changes, depression, or thoughts of harming yourself, a rash or allergic reaction (hives, swelling of face or throat, trouble breathing), signs of liver problems, or any unusual or bothersome side effect. Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first — stopping suddenly can be harmful.
when_it_works: This medicine starts working right away, but it may take several weeks to months before your viral load becomes very low (undetectable) and your CD4 count goes up. Most people notice improvements in lab results within a few weeks. You may not feel different at first, even when the medicine is working. It is very important to keep taking it every day even if you feel fine. Your doctor will check your blood regularly to make sure the medicine is working for you.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. There is a pregnancy registry for people who take HIV medicines — ask your doctor about it. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed if you have HIV, as you can pass the virus to your baby through breast milk. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease before starting this medicine. Children: This medicine can be used in children weighing at least 35 pounds (14 kg), but always follow your child's doctor's instructions. Older adults: Older patients may need more frequent monitoring for kidney and bone health.
